script: Before another return deadline slips past, let your AI help you check what is still eligible. Agents like Muse, Instinct, and dots need your approved access. Find recent purchases, check return policies, and list possible returns with deadlines and source links. Have it include order and delivery dates, item condition, fees, and anything it cannot verify, because a receipt on its own may not establish whether a return is still eligible. Sort the list by deadline, so a forgotten purchase does not disappear under another week of email. Then choose the item numbers and ask for a return request draft. Make it show the next step before sending anything, cancelling anything, or accepting a charge. For a pair of glasses, that means checking the exact policy, preparing the request, and showing you the next step. A return label depends on the retailer, and a request is not a refund. You still need to check the details and send the item back. The useful part is cutting down all that admin. For business software, audit upcoming renewals and check the contract before cancelling. I’m Hammad. Save this prompt, and follow for practical AI workflows you can actually use.

recording_caveat: app.screenrec is a fresh logged-out headless browser; it cannot inherit the owner’s signed-in app session. Public documentary selectors are unexecuted and require preflight. The local prompt-template selectors are controlled and have no backend or send button.
real_demo_remaining: For any claimed live agent demonstration, observe an authorized supported account, supply specifically approved/redacted sample receipts and a real retailer policy, run review-only analysis, inspect the actual result and record it. No outbound mail, live return, cancellation, fee acceptance, or label success should be simulated or performed by this task.
